property_summary: After a correctRState call triggered by BELOW_ONE with BASE_RESERVE_ < BASE_TARGET_, the state variable _BASE_TARGET_ must equal _BASE_RESERVE_ in the reference, but the buggy version fails to set it, so the equality breaks.

After any call to correctRState when the first condition is true, the reference sets _BASE_TARGET_ to _BASE_RESERVE_, while the buggy version leaves _BASE_TARGET_ unchanged, which can be detected by a subsequent call to getPMMState that reads the updated _BASE_TARGET_.

After correctRState executes under BELOW_ONE condition with BASE_RESERVE_ < BASE_TARGET_, the reference contract updates _BASE_TARGET_ to equal _BASE_RESERVE_, while the mutant leaves _BASE_TARGET_ unchanged, causing a discrepancy in subsequent getMidPrice() computation because getMidPrice calls getPMMState which relies on _BASE_TARGET_.

After correctRState transitions from BELOW_ONE to ONE (by resetting the state), a subsequent call to getMidPrice should return the same value as if getMidPrice were called immediately before the reset, because the new targets equal the reserves; the bug leaves _BASE_TARGET_ stale, which alters the mid-price calculation.
After correctRState triggers a BELOW_ONE -> ONE transition, the new _BASE_TARGET_ must equal _BASE_RESERVE_; the mutant omits this assignment, leaving _BASE_TARGET_ stale.

After correctRState resets RState from ABOVE_ONE to ONE, the reference updates _BASE_TARGET_ to match _BASE_RESERVE_, but the buggy version leaves _BASE_TARGET_ unchanged, so their _BASE_TARGET_ values differ after the call.

After correctRState resets RState from ABOVE_ONE to ONE, the reference updates _BASE_TARGET_ to _QUOTE_RESERVE_-adjusted value, but the buggy version leaves _BASE_TARGET_ unchanged; thus for any ABOVE_ONE state with _QUOTE_RESERVE_ < _QUOTE_TARGET_, only the reference correctly synchronizes _BASE_TARGET_.

After correctRState resets RState from ABOVE_ONE to ONE, the reference updates _BASE_TARGET_ to _BASE_RESERVE_, but the buggy version leaves _BASE_TARGET_ unchanged when _QUOTE_RESERVE_ < _QUOTE_TARGET_, so their _BASE_TARGET_ values differ.

After correctRState transitions RState from ABOVE_ONE to ONE (when _QUOTE_RESERVE_ < _QUOTE_TARGET_), the reference sets _BASE_TARGET_ equal to _BASE_RESERVE_, but the buggy version leaves _BASE_TARGET_ unchanged; therefore, for any admissible state where the transition triggers, the reference _BASE_TARGET_ equals _BASE_RESERVE_ after the call, while the buggy one does not.

After correctRState transitions from ABOVE_ONE to ONE (when _QUOTE_RESERVE_ < _QUOTE_TARGET_), the reference ensures _BASE_TARGET_ equals _BASE_RESERVE_, but the buggy version leaves _BASE_TARGET_ unchanged, so their _BASE_TARGET_ values differ post-call.

After correctRState sets RState to ONE when BELOW_ONE and BASE_RESERVE < BASE_TARGET, the reference ensures BASE_TARGET == BASE_RESERVE; the bug sets BASE_TARGET to QUOTE_RESERVE, breaking that invariant.
